intro: Extract G-code from 3MF pulls the sliced G-code out of a Bambu Studio or OrcaSlicer .gcode.3mf file, one per plate, together with each plate's thumbnail. It is useful to send the job to a non-Bambu printer, check it with Analyse G-code or G-code to image, or keep only what is going to be printed.

A .gcode.3mf is a ZIP with the project, the model and each plate's already-sliced G-code. You can extract all plates at once, in a ZIP, or only the one you choose by its number. If the file is an unsliced project 3MF, it has no G-code: slice it and save it as .gcode.3mf first.

Bambu G-code carries commands specific to its printers (AMS changes, calibrations); if you will use it on another machine, check it first with an editor and change the start and end. Thumbnails come out as PNG.
You can process up to ten files per task. They are processed on our server in the European Union and deleted automatically when they expire.

faq.q: Why does it say there is no G-code?
faq.a: Because it is an unsliced project 3MF. Slice it and export the plate as .gcode.3mf.

faq.q: Can I print it on a Prusa?
faq.a: Only by changing the start and end G-code, which are Bambu-specific; better slice the model for your printer.
AMS commands stay in the G-code as they are.

faq.q: How many plates can it have?
faq.a: As many as the project has; each plate comes with its number in the name.
Yes: OrcaSlicer saves the .gcode.3mf with the same structure as Bambu Studio.
